components.name: Default Button

components.description: Search field for concepts, aliases, topics, and domains.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" type="search" placeholder="Concept, alias, topic, domain" aria-label="Search concepts" />

components.name: Study Panel

narrative.overview:
Knowledge Review Agent is a focused study tool. It should feel like an atlas of ideas: dependable, navigable, and quiet enough for sustained reading. The graph provides orientation, while concept pages provide the actual learning surface.

The interface uses an ink-and-paper study character through dark readable text, cool paper-like neutrals, restrained blue interaction states, and lightly layered white surfaces.
keyCharacteristics: Lightly layered rather than heavily elevated.
Color carries domain meaning and never acts as the only signal.

rules.name: The Ink-and-Paper Rule
rules.body: Keep reading surfaces light and text dark. Do not use neon accents or low-contrast gray text for primary content.

rules.name: The Domain Signal Rule
rules.body: Domain color supports labels and graph nodes, but meaning must remain available through text, shape, or position.

rules.name: The Study-Length Rule
rules.body: Keep explanatory text readable at roughly 65-75 characters per line where layout permits. Use density for metadata and controls, not for core explanations.

rules.name: The Quiet Surface Rule
rules.body: Resting content should not float dramatically. Use elevation to clarify temporary overlays, not to decorate every section.

dos: Do use the ink, cool paper, surface white, and atlas border tokens consistently.
Do keep graph controls dense but labels explicit.
Do make provenance and relationships available without interrupting the primary learning flow.
Do preserve keyboard focus, readable contrast, responsive reflow, and reduced-motion behavior.
Do use domain colors as supporting signals, never as the only source of meaning.
donts: Don't build cluttered dashboards or add unexplained metrics.
Don't use neon colors, decorative gradients, or visual effects that compete with study content.
Don't use large shadows on resting panels.
Don't rely on color alone for domain or relationship meaning.
Don't let presentation refinement alter technical content, equations, citations, or provenance.
